answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontrivial deposit before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation changes. The protocol weights influence by stake and slashes deposits when an identity is proven to have double-claimed or colluded, using signed, auditable records as evidence. An atlas of linked claims can help an anchor agent trace a coordinated plume of accounts, but the core cost is unavoidable: an attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, so multiplying fake identities is expensive.
